title: Portfolio Manager
leads: The operators on your sites, one for every ten phones, and the site lead on every floor with 20 or more phones.
where: On the floor of the sites in your book, in one hub area, moving between them every day
hours: Clock-in at 7:00 AM, evening check-outs checked by 6:00 PM, six days a week
summary: You own a book of sites in one hub area and the hours they record every month.

posting.headline: Portfolio Manager (site operations), Cairo
posting.about: KMSC runs the field operations behind a large artificial intelligence project, at industrial sites across Cairo. You own a book of sites in one hub area, with their operators, site leads, devices, and monthly target, and you report to the Director of Operations. You work on the floor, and you start with two weeks as an operator.
do: Lead the operators and site leads on every site in your book.
Visit every site in your book without warning, at least once a day.
Answer every quality flag within 24 hours, so the worker gets the fix the same day.
Handle absences and no-shows, as the first response to any problem on the floor.
Review the day's field data at 5:00 PM, then check each site's evening check-out form by 6:00 PM.
Find the next site for your book, and run its launch day with the Commercial Director.
need: Ready to spend two weeks as an operator first.
Able to lead a small team and give a correction calmly, in person.
On your feet, moving between sites, six days a week.
Careful with numbers and on time with a report, every day.
plus: You have been an operator on one of our sites.
You have led a team on a factory, warehouse, or construction floor.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Paid training: two weeks as an operator, then one week beside a Portfolio Manager.
Your own book of sites and a clear monthly target, in a company that writes everything down.
A referral bonus when a site you found signs, and a book that grows with every site you bring in.
posting.apply: Send your name, age, where you live, a phone number, and where you have worked. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Portfolio Manager at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Director of Operations.
Your start date is {start}. Your first two weeks are paid training as an operator. Then one week with {manager} and a Portfolio Manager, before you take your own book.

terms.label: Place of work
terms.v: Based at {site}, moving between the sites in your book, in one hub area

terms.label: Hours
terms.v: Clock-in at 7:00 AM, evening check-outs checked by 6:00 PM, six days a week

terms.label: Pay
terms.v: {pay} per month, paid at the end of the month

conditions: A copy of your national ID.
Your signature on the rules, the consent form, and the fraud briefing.
One account in your own name. Accounts are never shared.
expect: You are on a site at 7:00 AM every working day.
Every site's evening check-out is in by 6:00 PM and checked by you. Every flag is answered within 24 hours.
Every phone in your book is counted, morning and evening.
offer.closing: Please sign below to accept this offer. We look forward to working with you.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for accepted hours. Your book has a monthly target. Those hours come from operators who show up, phones that are counted, and workers who hear about a flag in time. You own all three, and you own the next site in your book. Nothing on your floors waits for someone else.
outcomes: Your book reaches its monthly hour target.
Every flag on your sites is closed within 24 hours, and the fix holds.
Every phone is counted morning and evening. Every site's evening check-out form is in by 6:00 PM, and you have checked it.
Your book grows. You find the next site, Adham closes it, Mano papers it.
daily: 7:00 AM. Count with the site lead on every floor with 20 or more phones. Clock in with your operators. A phone missing now is your call at 7:05.
During the shift. Visit every site without warning. Angles, restarts, charging, who has which phone. The site lead holds the floor between visits.
A flag lands. Tell Moharam within the hour. Show the worker the video and say the fix.
Any hour. Absence, broken phone, site below target: fix it or call Moharam within the hour.
4:00 PM. Take the handover and match the morning count.
5:00 PM. Watch every session. Delete what must not go out. 6:00 PM. The site lead submits the evening check-out form. You check it.
8:00 PM. You know who is absent tomorrow and who covers.
weekly: Thursday, 4:00 PM. The three-way count: registry, MDM, and room say the same number.
Once a week. Your book is checked against its target. Bring the cause and the fix.
Once a week. One call or one visit toward the next site for your book.
monthly: Go through the month's flags with each operator and site lead. Interview for any open site lead seat.
standards: A correction is given in person, with the video open. Say what right looks like.
No phone before screening: ID showing 18 or older, signed consent, fraud sign-off, own account.
A phone is on a head, on charge, or in the provided bag, signed for.
You find a site. Adham closes it. Mano papers it.
Money to Ahmed Alaa, gear to the Planning and Logistics Lead, quality to Youssef Medhat, papers to Mano. Nobody contacts the client.
never: Three flags remove a worker the same shift, whatever the site needs.
A phone that goes home, or an account that is shared, ends the job.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: An operator on one of our sites. Ten phones, every round, every count.
With Moharam and a Portfolio Manager. A real evening check-out checked, one flag closed, one worker screened, one site lead interviewed.
Your own book. Two evening check-outs accepted in a row, and Moharam signs your training.

measures: Accepted hours in your book, against the monthly target.
Flags closed within 24 hours, per week.
The Thursday count: every difference explained the same day.
Evening check-outs in by 6:00 PM and checked, every site, every day.
handbook.call: Moharam, for anything on the floor. The Planning and Logistics Lead for gear, a run, or a hub. Ahmed Alaa for money. Youssef Medhat for a flag. Mano for papers. An injury or the police: Moharam, then Adham.
